articles.title: Mykhailo Mudryk transfer news: Tottenham sign Chelsea winger on loan as Tosin joins in permanent deal
articles.summary: Spurs sign Mykhailo Mudryk on loan from Chelsea; Tottenham have an option to buy the winger, who has not played a competitive game since November 2024 due to a doping ban that was resolved in July; Spurs also sign defender Tosin from Chelsea in £12m deal as Kevin Danso replacement
articles.body:
Mudryk has not played a competitive game since November 2024 due to a doping ban that was resolved in July.

The 25-year-old joined Chelsea for £88.5m in January 2023 amid much fanfare, with the Blues beating Arsenal to his signing.

But the Ukraine international failed to live up to that price tag at Stamford Bridge and will now look to reignite his career in north London.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi coached Mudryk at Shakhtar Donetsk and even tipped him as a future Ballon d'Or winner.

Mudryk has been followed at Spurs by Chelsea team-mate Tosin , who has joined in a £12m deal.

Spurs will pay £10m up front for the defender, with £2m in add-ons.

The 28-year-old is a replacement for Kevin Danso , who moved to Sunderland on a season-long loan.

There is a £22m obligation to make the move permanent if the Black Cats avoid relegation this season.

'I'm so excited to be reunited with De Zerbi'

Mudryk, who will wear the number 27 shirt at Spurs, said: "It's a great feeling. I can't wait to start training and playing for the club, and I'm so excited to be reunited with Roberto De Zerbi.

"I'm a player who brings speed and creativity, and I want to help in both the offensive and defensive areas. I want to make the fans excited.

"I can see it's a strong squad here with good players, and I'm looking forward to sharing a pitch and special moments with them."

De Zerbi added: "Having worked with Misha earlier in his career, I know exactly what he can bring to our team.

"He has the quality to change a game with his speed and ability in one-vs-one situations, and is an exciting, attacking talent.

"I will demand a lot from Misha and it is our job to help him find the best version of himself. If we do that then he can become a very important player for us. I am very happy he chose to come here, and I cannot wait to work with him again."

Spurs sporting director, Johan Lange, said: "We believe he [Mudryk] has the attributes to make a real contribution to our team and we are excited to see his development in our environment.

"Mykhailo's ambition and determination to take on this challenge has impressed me. He has a strong desire to succeed and improve, and that fits well with the culture we are building.

"We will fully support Mykhailo as he settles in, works with Roberto and our coaching staff and his new teammates, and we look forward to this next chapter of his career."

Mudryk was suspended for four years for failing a drug test, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, two years ago.

Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) while changes to World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) procedures in the interim mean that had his failed test produced the same result now, charges would not have been brought.

The FA said: "Changes have been made… which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, the FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the ADRVs (Anti-Doping Rule Violations) charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement.

"Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

articles.title: El Como pone la guinda al pastel: 40 millones por Moise Kean
articles.standfirst: El delantero italiano llega desde la Fiorentina
articles.summary: El delantero italiano llega desde la Fiorentina
articles.body: El mercado del Como 1907 de Cesc Fàbregas está dando que hablar hasta el último minuto. Y lo mejor, lo han dejado para el final. Tras abrir la sesión estival de transferencias confirmando la permanencia de Nico Paz a cambio de 60 millones de euros, los lombardos incorporan a su '9': Moise Kean. El internacional italiano llega desde la Fiorentina en una operación valorada en 40 millones entre parte fija y bonus. "Por fin estoy aquí", ha asegurado nada más pisar el centro de entrenamiento del Como. El internacional italiano, de 26 años, llega cedido a cambio de 10 millones de euros. Sin embargo, el Como deberá abordar una opción de compra obligatoria fijada en 25 kilos. Podría pagar, además, otros 5 millones en concepto de bonus. Tras la salida de Morata, Cesc ya tiene delantero que acompañe a un Douvikas que anotó 14 goles el pasado curso y suma dos esta temporada en dos jornadas. Pero Kean es elevar la apuesta, y hacerlo de forma muy elevada. El canterano de la Juve tocó techo en la 2024-25 firmando una temporada estratosférica en la que anotó 25 goles. Ahora, tras una 2025-26 más discreta (9 goles) en la que la Fiorentina peleó por no descender, debe recuperar ese nivel de la mano de Fàbregas y en uno de los equipos con un juego más atractivo del 'Calcio': el Como. Todavía está por ver si el Como amplía su mercado con algún refuerzo de última hora (suena Robert Sánchez para la portería) pero el que ha reaccionado ha sido la Fiore: los 'Viola' reemplazan a su delantero con Willy Gnonto (ex Leeds, internacional italiano) y Beto (Everton).

articles.title: Belocian, refuerzo para la defensa racinguista
articles.standfirst: El ex del Bayern Leverkusen permanecerá en el conjunto cántabro por una temporada
articles.summary: El ex del Bayern Leverkusen permanecerá en el conjunto cántabro por una temporada
articles.body: El Racing ha conseguido la cesión del defensa francés Jeanuël Belocian procedente del Bayer Leverkusen hasta el 30 de junio del 2027. El jugador, que actúa principalmente como defensa central, ha disputado 27 partidos en la Bundesliga, 31 en la Ligue 1 gala, cuatro en la Champions League y seis en la Europa League. El Racing ya contaba con cuatro centrales, Pablo Ramón, Manu Hernando, Pedro Felipe y Facu González, además de Mantilla y Salinas que pueden ocupar dicha posición. Jeanuël Belocian nació en Les Abymes (Guadalupe- Francia) el 17 de febrero de 2005 y comenzó su trayectoria profesional en el Stade Rennes, con el que debutó en la máxima categoría gala ante el Metz -con solo 17 años- el 20 de marzo de 2022. El curso siguiente el zaguero se estrenó en la Europa League y uno después fue traspasado al Bayer Leverkusen, aunque desde enero a junio de 2026 militó cedido en el VFL Wolfsburgo.

articles.title: El Real Madrid sigue haciendo caja: el Brighton paga 23 millones por Chema Andrés
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, que consevaban el 50% de los derechos del jugador, recibirán 11,5 kilos
articles.summary: Los blancos, que consevaban el 50% de los derechos del jugador, recibirán 11,5 kilos
articles.body: La 'Fábrica' sigue haciendo 'caja'. A los 66 millones que ha pagado el Como por Nico Paz, los 50 que ha desembolsado el Fulham por Gonzalo García (40) y César Palacios (10), los 10 que ha abonado el Estrasburgo por Jacobo Ortega... se suman ahora los 23 que ha gastado el Brighton & Hove Albion para firmar a José María Andrés Baixauli (Bétera, 2005). Chema Andrés, como se conoce futbolísticamente al mediocentro formado en Valdebebas, se marchó el pasado verano traspasado al Stuttgart a cambio de 6 millones de euros. Sin embargo, el Real Madrid se reservó el 50% de los derechos del futbolista, por lo que recibirá 11,5 kilos de su traspaso al Brighton. Ahora es el Stuttgart el que se reserva un porcentaje sobre una futura venta del internacional sub 21, mientras que el Real Madrid pierde definitivamente el control del jugador. Chema Andrés, de 21 años y 1,90 metros de altura, completó una buena temporada en su debut en la Bundesliga con el Stuttgart. El español disputó un total de 39 encuentros (1.939') entre todas las competiciones. Además, evidenció su poderío en la jugadas a balón parado. Cerró el curso con un total de cuatro goles, tres en Liga, y dos asistencias. Chema Andrés se convierte en la décima incorporación del Brighton, especializado en captar talento joven. Las 'gaviotas' han gastado 166,5 millones en Luka Vuskovic (Tottenham/54 millones), Zadok Yohanna (AIK/28), Pascal Struijk (Leeds/23,2), Chema Andrés (Stuttgart/23), Jaouen Hadjam (Young Boys/13), Costinha (Olympiacos/12,7), Michael Svoboda (Venezia/5), Matías Orozco (Deportivo Cali/4,1), Rodrigo Rego (Benfica/3,5) y Promise David (Union Saint-Gilloise).

articles.title: Oficial: El Elche adquiere los servicios de Rubén Sánchez
articles.standfirst: El lateral diestro llega procedente del Espanyol por medio millón de euros
articles.summary: El lateral diestro llega procedente del Espanyol por medio millón de euros
articles.body: En el último día de mercado, pero el Elche adquiere una de sus ambiciones del verano: Rubén Sánchez. El lateral diestro de 25 años llega procedente del Espanyol a cambio de 500.000 euros. La entidad barcelonesa se queda con el 25% de una plusvalía, en el caso de una futura venta del jugador. Rubén Sánchez firma por tres temporadas, hasta junio de 2029, con opción de ampliar su vinculación por una campaña más. Rubén Sánchez Sáez (Barcelona, 04/02/2001) es un lateral/carrilero derecho de perfil ofensivo. Aparte de la necesidad franjiverde de reforzar la banda diestra, el futbolista catalán estaba fuera de los planes del entrenador del Espanyol, Manolo González. De hecho, ni siquiera entró en la convocatoria de los tres primeros partidos de esta temporada. En la campaña anterior, disputó 22 compromisos, aunque sólo nueve como titular y dos completos. Canterano perico, será su tercera experiencia fuera del Espanyol, tras sus fructíferas cesiones a Mirandés y Granada en Segunda. Eso sí, ahora ya queda desvinculado del Espanyol. “Rubén Sánchez destaca por su capacidad para desenvolverse en el lateral derecho, su intensidad y su compromiso en las dos fases del juego. Su recorrido y experiencia en el fútbol profesional le permiten aportar alternativas tanto en labores defensivas como en sus incorporaciones al ataque”, describe el Elche en su anuncio oficial. El interés del club ilicitano por Rubén Sánchez ha estado presente durante todo el mercado, pero finalmente se ha cerrado en el ‘deadline’. Este movimiento es el primero que el Elche oficializa en el último día de mercado. Se esperan varios más, con la necesidad de refuerzos después de empezar la liga con un punto de nueve posibles.

articles.summary: Vivianne Miedema will miss the start of the Women's Super League season because of a knee injury.
articles.body:
Manchester City striker Vivianne Miedema will miss the beginning of the Women's Super League season with a knee injury.

It is understood that Netherlands international Miedema, 30, has not suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

The club said the latest issue is also "separate to the previous knee injuries she's experienced".

Miedema scored 10 times and assisted five more in the league last term as City won the Women's Super League for the first time since 2016.

She had a largely injury-free campaign last year, although she underwent knee surgery at the end of the season.

The season begins on Friday, when London City Lionesses host Manchester United (19:00 BST). Manchester City's first game is on Sunday, when they host promoted Birmingham City (14:30 BST).

articles.title: Rangers: Nicolas Raskin 'as good as gold' amid transfer wait - Derek McInnes
articles.summary: Nicolas Raskin has "been good as gold" despite no signs of a transfer from Rangers and the Belgium midfielder's absence from their latest two match-day squads, manager Derek McInnes insists.
articles.body:
Nicolas Raskin has "been good as gold" despite no signs of a transfer from Rangers and the Belgium midfielder's absence from their latest two match-day squads, manager Derek McInnes has stressed.

The 25-year-old was widely expected to be sold after starring at the World Cup, but there have been no bids yet that have piqued Rangers' interest.

Raskin signed a four-and-a-half-year contract when he joined the Scottish Premiership club from Standard Liege in January 2023.

"Nico's been first-class since he came back from the World Cup - he's been good as gold, he's trained brilliantly," McInnes insisted on Sky Sports as he looked forward to Wednesday's visit to Falkirk.

What are big questions in final two days of Scottish transfer window?

Why is Scotland's transfer window closing on Thursday?

Who has your Premiership club brought in & let go this summer?

"Obviously there's been a lot of chat about potential interest and there's been a lot of conversations had with the club and prospective buyers.

"But, until an offer comes in that the club need to consider, Nico just has to knuckle down and train.

"I've no doubts that, if the window closes and Nico's still a Rangers player, he'll give brilliant service as he's done previously. He's getting interest because he's a good player. I want to work with good players. We just needs to wait and see how things develop."

As for incomings, McInnes indicated that Rangers are likely to make just one more signing before Thursday's transfer deadline, with Kevin Kelsy reportedly close to a move from Portland Timbers.

The 22-year-old Venezuelan forward appears to be the Ibrox club's choice as a replacement for Youssef Chermiti, who suffered a long-term injury last month just as the Portuguese was subject of major transfer interest.

"We're still working hard to get one in at the minute," McInnes said. "We're getting closer on that one, but we believe it's only going to be the one in.

"If we can get a striker in, that helps alleviate the disappointment of Youssef's injury. I think that would be pretty important for us.

"It wasn't something we were looking to do, so you've got to weigh everything up both from a financial and a numbers point of view in terms of the squad."

Rangers have already signed 12 players this summer in addition to recruiting McInnes himself from Heart of Midlothian.

"I think the club have made the right improvements in certain areas and I think we've had a lot of good work done," he said.

"I'm saying one – you never know, it might be more than one – but, if we can get the one in that we want, it certainly helps alleviate a problem we've got at the minute."

The Ibrox exit door is likely to be busier before Thursday's deadline, with midfielder Lyall Cameron having already joined Dundee United on loan and winger Ross McCausland, striker Bojan Miovski, and defenders John Souttar and Clinton Nsiala among others linked with moves away.

"On players out, there's been a few conversations had," McInnes said. "There may well be things developing over the next 24-48 hours on that front."

articles.title: LaLiga defiende su modelo: "En el año 2012 no se pagaba ni al electricista"
articles.standfirst: Javier Gómez, director general corporativo de LaLiga, habla del mercado y de la comparación con la Premier
articles.summary: Javier Gómez, director general corporativo de LaLiga, habla del mercado y de la comparación con la Premier
articles.body: Javier Gómez, director general corporativo de LaLiga, compareció ante los medios en el último día del mercado de fichajes, como hace habitualmente. El padre del control económico defendió el modelo de LaLiga respecto al de la Premier y explicó cómo ha podido fichar el Deportivo, recién ascendido, a Aubameyang, Adama Traoré, Angeliño o Giménez, entre otros. Cifras del mercado: "Este año vamos a estar por encima unos 120 millones del año pasado, entre 750 y 800 millones. Y este año ha habido menos ventas. Cuando terminemos va a haber menos ventas que compras". LaLiga, modelo de cantera: "Los valores de LaLiga básicamente son la cantera. Se basan en la cantera, es un modelo basado en eso. Es como se viene estructurando no solo este año, los años anteriores también". Deportivo: "Acaban de ascender, tendrán una idea de consolidarse en la primera categoría. Poniendo el dinero máximo que se puede poner. Es público que ha hecho ampliación de capital, como el Atlético de Madrid. Ha puesto el dinero su máximo accionista". Premier: "La Bundesliga está como nosotros. Si la Premier tiene el doble de ingresos que nosotros, debería tener el doble de inversión. Deberían invertir unos 1.500 millones, están invirtiendo 3.500 millones. Ese dinero viene de los accionistas. ¿Qué implica? Varias cuestiones. Una, que es una cuestión solo de la Premier, que es un modelo de pérdidas permanente. Tiene otras consecuencias, que es que inflaciona todo el sector, la Bundesliga, la liga francesa y a nosotros. Esto es lo que provoca excederte en demasía de lo que generan las cuentas de los clubes. Los precios que están pagando están por encima de lo que genera el sector. Se ha creado un órgano en Inglaterra que va a controlar los clubes de la Premier y el resto de categorías. Mientras se pone en marcha todo sigue igual. No es bueno para el sector en general ni para LaLiga, que nos afecta. Atlético: "Las ampliaciones de capital funcionan... esto que voy a explicar es para el Atlético de Madrid y para el resto. El Atlético de Madrid lo que ha hecho es que con la ampliación de capital tiene la posibilidad de incrementar su límite de manera simple por el importa de la ampliación dividido entre todos, básicamente, de una manera muy resumida, con el máximo del 25% de su cifra de negocio. Es decir, no puedes incrementar tu límite más de un 25% de tu cifra de negocio. El Atlético ha hecho el mismo procedimiento. Si amplías 100, 50 puedes utilizarlo para incrementar tu límite". Modelo de LaLiga: "Nosotros aquí nos fijamos en nosotros, no tenemos complejos. Aquí los clubes decidieron, por de dónde se partía. Recuerdo que en el año 2012, yo me acuerdo perfectamente, los que estábamos, esto era una ruina. No se pagaba no solo a los jugadores, no se pagaba al electricista, no se pagaba a la azafata, no se pagaba a los empleados, no se pagaba a nadie. Decidieron los clubes una cosa tan sencilla como vamos a imponernos nuestras reglas, vamos a gastar hasta donde podamos. Y nos dará hasta donde nos dé. Pasa por hacer inversiones que generen más, explotar nuestros recursos... pero con la premisa de que los clubes sean sostenibles en el largo plazo. Si un accionista se va, el club siga teniendo futuro. No creemos en modelos que sean a pérdidas permanentes, porque no solo afecta a quien lo hace, sino al resto de competiciones también".

images.caption: Javier Tebas y Javier Gómez, en un acto de LaLiga. EFE

articles.title: Congelación de óvulos: la RFEF en defensa de la maternidad
articles.standfirst: La iniciativa pionera de la federación se aplaude, pero expertas apuntan que no es la panacéa y que "no hay que olvidar la reproducción natural"
articles.summary: La iniciativa pionera de la federación se aplaude, pero expertas apuntan que no es la panacéa y que "no hay que olvidar la reproducción natural"
articles.body: La maternidad ya no está fuera de juego. La Federación Española de Fútbol presentará el 21 de este mes un acuerdo con la Clínica Tambre por el que las futbolistas internacionales que hayan formado parte de alguna convocatoria de la selección desde la última NationsLeague en adelante podrán congelar sus óvulos acogiéndose a este programa. La medida, pionera en el deporte español, favorecerá que las futbolistas no tengan que renunciar al deseo de ser madres por su profesión, medida de presente y futuro, pues cada vez se extiende más la carrera deportiva que coincide en tiempos con la época más fértil de las mujeres. “Desde luego que hay una parte muy positiva”, advierte Patricia Bartolomé, directora del único máster en fertilidad integrativa que hay en España. “Pero es un titular muy peligroso que se diga que congelar los óvulos es garantía de fecundidad futura”. La terapeuta advierte que aunque se vitrifiquen los óvulos, “no congelas tu útero, tu cuerpo, tu maternidad... Luego hay un proceso largo en un cuerpo que ya no es el mismo. Hay que fecundar ese óvulo, tiene que madurar, tiene que implantarse, luego ese embrión tiene que crecer favorablemente, una gestación de nueve meses”. Y arroja un dato que recalca no es categórico, pero sí significativo. “En 2022 había en España más de 300.000 óvulos congelados y sólo nacieron por este método 350 niños. Evidentemente no todos se implantaron: unos perma- necieron en ese estado, otros eran inservibles, otros más no fecundaron. Lo que quiero que entiendan es que sólo es una posibilidad más de reproducción, no una garantía de que si congelas 20 óvulos tienes 20 fetos en potencia. Porque luego puede no servir ninguno y esa falsa expectativa tiene que paliarse con información”. Se evitaría así, dice la experta, “un coste emocional que, en caso de no dar resultado, suele ser muy complicado. Se vende demasiado bonito”. Nunca hasta ahora una federación había ido tan lejos. La WNBA, la liga profesional estadounidense de baloncesto, fue pionera inspirada en las políticas de empresas como Facebook y Apple. Cuando el sindicato de jugadoras firmó su convenio colectivo en 2019, incluyó la opción de que las veteranas fueran reembolsadas hasta 20.000 dólares al año por gastos de adopción, subrogación, congelación de óvulos o tratamientos de fertilidad. En convenios posteriores esa cifra se amplió: los últimos acuerdos elevaron el reembolso hasta 60.000. Lo han copiado algunos clubes de fútbol. En esa línea, las tenistas de la WTA tienen acceso a becas para tratamientos de fertilidad, incluida la congelación de óvulos y la fecundación in vitro, dentro de la nueva política de maternidad, con clasificación protegida al volver. “Lo ideal”, remata Bartolomé, “es que el deporte se adaptara a la mujer y no la mujer al deporte. Tenemos un problema social. Queremos camibar la realidad biológica, pero de momento no es posible. Es una técnica que se inició hace 40 años como alternativa a una fertilidad amenazada por un cáncer o similar, pero ahora se quiere medicalizar a todas las mujeres. No hay que olvidarse de la reproducción natural. El cuerpo tiene unos tiempos y unas respuestas. Se le puede intentar engañar, pero a veces funciona y otras veces no. Y esto no es por una cuestión religiosa o moda. Es pura biología”.

articles.title: El Elche ficha a Roy Revivo hasta 2030
articles.standfirst: El lateral izquierdo israelí llega procedente del Maccabi Tel Aviv para reforzar la banda zurda del conjunto franjiverde
articles.summary: El lateral izquierdo israelí llega procedente del Maccabi Tel Aviv para reforzar la banda zurda del conjunto franjiverde
articles.body: El Elche ya tiene nuevo refuerzo para su lateral izquierdo. El conjunto franjiverde ha alcanzado un acuerdo con el Maccabi Tel Aviv para el traspaso de Roy Revivo, que firma con el club ilicitano hasta junio de 2030. Nacido en Israel el 22 de mayo de 2003, Revivo aterriza en el fútbol español después de desarrollar toda su carrera en su país. El defensa se ha convertido en uno de los jugadores destacados del Maccabi Tel Aviv y llega al Elche con experiencia tanto en la competición doméstica como en el fútbol europeo. Internacional absoluto con Israel, el nuevo lateral franjiverde destaca especialmente por su recorrido, velocidad y vocación ofensiva. Es un futbolista capaz de ocupar toda la banda y participar con frecuencia en las acciones de ataque, donde aporta profundidad y capacidad para generar peligro desde el costado. Revivo ha dado un paso adelante durante la última temporada y se ha consolidado como una pieza importante del Maccabi Tel Aviv. Su llegada al Elche supone además su primera experiencia en el fútbol español, donde afrontará el reto de competir en LaLiga EA Sports. Con 23 años, el israelí se incorpora a un proyecto que busca seguir completando su plantilla con juventud y talento. El Elche encuentra en Revivo un lateral con margen de crecimiento y recorrido internacional para apuntalar una de las posiciones del equipo de cara a la nueva temporada.

articles.title: Texas A&M QB Marcel Reed Talks 'Hate' for Texas, Makes Bold Prediction for Rivalry Game
articles.summary: Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed didn't hold back on how he feels about the Texas Longhorns during an interview with Blake Toppmeyer of USA Today.
articles.body:
Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed didn't hold back on how he feels about the Texas Longhorns during an interview with Blake Toppmeyer of USA Today .

"We don't like Texas. I don't like Texas," Reed told Toppmeyer. "It sucks that we've lost to them twice. But, they're coming here this year, so they're gonna have to pay. I've got something for them, for sure."

Reed also had this to say about Texas' burnt orange color.

"I hate the color orange," Reed said. "The colors just look so ugly. Everywhere you go (in Austin), you see that color orange. Burnt orange? Who likes burnt orange? Texas, it's the rival, bro. You gotta hate them."

Aside from the fact that the two schools are bitter in-state rivals, Reed has good reason to dislike Texas. The Aggies have endured rough losses to Texas in both 2024 and 2025 with Reed calling signals both times.

In 2024, Texas A&M lost 17-7 at home. The Aggies were shut out offensively, and their only points came after Will Lee III's third-quarter pick-six.

In 2025, the No. 3 Aggies were favored over the Longhorns, but Texas quarterback Archie Manning led his team to a 27-17 victory. Reed had a tough game through the air, tossing a pair of interceptions and no touchdowns.

Reed has shown promise as Texas A&M's QB1, accounting for 53 touchdowns in his two seasons as a starter (40 passing, 13 rushing), 5,033 passing yards (8.2 yards per attempt) and 1,036 rushing yards.

Last year's Aggies team went 11-0 before losing its final two games, including a 10-3 defeat to Miami in the College Football Playoff.

This year's Aggies team has great expectations again and sits eighth in the Associated Press preseason poll . Texas is a few notches higher at No. 5. This matchup could be a heated and crucially important game when they meet again soon enough.

That'll be on Friday, Nov. 27, when the Aggies welcome the Longhorns to Kyle Field in College Station.

articles.title: Ethan Nwaneri, otra 'joya' para el Borussia Dortmund
articles.standfirst: El extremo del Arsenal llega cedido por una temporada sin opción de compra
articles.summary: El extremo del Arsenal llega cedido por una temporada sin opción de compra
articles.body: El Borussia Dortmund continúa fiel a su política de apostar por talento joven. El 'BVB' ha cerrado la incorporación de Ethan Chidiebere Nwaneri (Islington, 2007). El debutante más joven en la historia de la Premier League (15 años y 181 días) recala cedido por una temporada en el Signal Iduna Park procedente del Arsenal. Cedido... sin opción de compra. "Necesita jugar al fútbol", había advertido Mikel Arteta ante la competencia que Nwaneri tenía en el Emirates con Eberechi Eze, Martin Odegaard e, incluso, el joven Max Dowman. Nwaneri, que demandaba más minutos, ya jugó cedido en el Olympique de Marsella en el tramo final de la temporada pasada. Con el 'OM' disputó 11 partidos, marcó dos goles y repartió una asistencia. El inglés, internacional sub 21, se convierte en la séptima incorporación de un Borussia Dortmund que ha gastado 108,5 millones en fichajes. Nwaneri se suma a Konstantinos Karetsas (Genk/30 millones), Giannis Konstantelias (PAOK/26), Joey Veerman (PSV/22), Joane Gadou (Salzburgo/19,5), Kaua Prates (Cruzeiro/7) y Justin Lerma (Independiente del Valle/4). El extremo/mediapunta del Arsenal era un 'viejo' objeto de deseo del Borussia Dortmund. Sin embargo, su incorporación se ha acelerado después de que el recién llegado Konstantelias sufriera una lesión de larga duración en su debut contra el Hamburgo.

articles.standfirst: El extremo senegalés llega al Etihad desde el Everton
articles.summary: El extremo senegalés llega al Etihad desde el Everton
articles.body: Se esperaba un cierre de mercado caliente por parte del Manchester City después de ser protagonistas en la operación salida... y los del Etihad, ahora con Enzo Maresca a los mandos, no han decepcionado. A la espera de saber qué pasa con Enzo Fernández y sin la posibilidad de fichar a Gakpo ya sobre la mesa... el que llega al norte de Inglaterra es Iliman Ndiaye. El City va a pagar a sus vecinos del Everton una cifra superior a los 70 millones de euros entre parte fija y bonus. Los 'sky blues' han superado la competencia del Tottenham y, además, deberían mandar a Jack Grealish en dirección contraria... de vuelta al Merseyside. Ndiaye, formado en el fútbol inglés entre el Boreham Wood y el Sheffield United, 'despegó' mediáticamente en Francia, su país natal. Todo después de firmar un curso impresionante en el Sheffield, en Championship, con 25 goles generados desde el extremo. En 2024, el Everton pagaba 18 millones de euros al Marsella por Ndiaye... y ahora, dos años después, lo vende por más de 70 'kilos'. Maresca suma, de este modo, un jugador tremendamente polivalente. Ndiaye puede desempeñarse como extremo en ambas bandas y, también, jugar por dentro.

El ahora futbolista del Paok Salónica estará contento con esta decisión y, como un veterano ya que es, le habrá aconsejado desde la distancia como lo hacía cuando ambos compartían vestuario: "Jonma, súbete los pantalones".

articles.title: Pablo García, rumbo al Racing de Santander por 5,5 millones
articles.standfirst: El canterano bético apunta al conjunto cántabro, que comprará el 50% de sus derechos
articles.summary: El canterano bético apunta al conjunto cántabro, que comprará el 50% de sus derechos
articles.body: La operación salida en el Betis continúa. Después de ceder a Petit al Cádiz, y a la espera de conocer el futuro de Iker Losada, que podría salir a alguno de los mercados que sigan abiertos más allá de este martes, los verdiblancos están ultimando el traspaso de Pablo García al Racing de Santander. El conjunto cántabro, tal y como ha avanzado El Desmarque, abonará si termina concretándose la operación unos 5,5 millones de euros por el 50% de los derechos económicos del atacante, que buscará en El Sardinero el protagonismo del que no estaba gozando con Pellegrini desde su salto al primer equipo. Pablo García ha sido uno de los nombres propios del mercado bético durante todo el verano. En especial tras recibir una suculenta propuesta del Hull City para jugar en la Premier League. Sin embargo, el conjunto inglés no alcanzó las cantidades solicitadas por el Betis para dar el visto bueno a la operación. El Olympiacos también se interesó hace algunos días por el talentoso futbolista sevillano y aunque sí ofrecía un traspaso más elevado que convencía al club andaluz, no terminaba de seducir al futbolista para poner rumbo a Grecia. En las horas finales de mercado ha sido el Racing de Santander el equipo que todo apunta a que terminará haciéndose con los servicios de Pablo. En este traspaso, el Betis logrará una plusvalía de 5,5 millones, el total de la operación al tratarse de un jugador formado en sus categorías inferiores y que irá directa a compensar las pérdidas del pasado curso, y conserva la mitad de los derechos económicos en caso de futura venta. Un movimiento que, en parte, ayuda también a que sea posible la inscripción de Dani Ceballos.

articles.title: Premier League clubs set new transfer spending record
articles.summary: Premier League clubs break their all-time summer transfer record after spending reaches £3.198bn.
articles.body:
Premier League clubs have broken their all-time summer transfer record after spending reached £3.198bn.

English top flight clubs had already pushed well beyond the £3bn barrier when Iliman Ndiaye's move from Everton to Manchester City on deadline day for an initial £60m took the amount spent past the previous mark of £3.14bn from 12 months ago.

The amount dwarfs the £1.13bn spent by clubs just five years ago and underlines the power top English clubs have to attract talent, according to figures provided to BBC Sport by Paul Macdonald, founder of FootballTransfers.com.

Follow live coverage of transfer deadline day

Find all the latest football transfers on our dedicated page

Four of the 11 most expensive signings in the history of football have happened this summer – with three of them being Premier League signings.

And Liverpool paid an initial £106m , which could rise to £123m, for Paris St-Germain and France forward Bradley Barcola.

Yan Diomande's move to Real Madrid and Anthony Gordon's switch from Newcastle to Barcelona are the only deals completed so far this summer by clubs outside the Premier League to involve fees in excess of £60m.

Tottenham 's acquisition of Sandro Tonali was a club-record fee which could reach £100m, while the north London club have also spent heavily on Mateus Fernandes (£85m) from West Ham and Savio from Manchester City (£75m potentially rising to £85m).

Other transfers around this range include the £85.6m deal that City struck to bring in Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille , Bruno Guimaraes' arrival at Arsenal for £75m from Newcastle , and Manchester United landing Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton for £70m.

So maybe it is not surprising then that in the compilation of the 20 most expensive transfers completed that only six were not to clubs in the English top flight.

Indeed, newly-promoted Ipswich Town have spent more on new signings than the likes of Barcelona, AC Milan, Juventus and reigning European champions PSG.

Premier League keeping its deals in house

This summer, 38% of deals involving a transfer fee have been from one Premier League club to another, which is an increase from last year, when the figure was 30%.

That then increases to 48% in instances where Premier League clubs have bought players from lower down the English football pyramid.

On top of that, the Premier League net spend remains over £1bn for this window - by far the most in Europe - despite many of the biggest sales this summer coming from the English league too. Bundesliga and Ligue 1 clubs have received more in transfer fees than they have spent.

Aside from French-based duo Barcola and Bouaddi, the majority of major signings made by Premier League clubs this month have been from rival clubs in the same division.

They include England team-mates Rogers and Anderson, while Newcastle sold Tonali to Spurs and Guimaraes to Arsenal .

Manchester United snapped up Baleba from Brighton after a 12-month chase to aid their midfield revamp, while Tottenham 's recruitment of Fernandes and Savio is in the same category.

But why are English clubs buying each other's players more than ever this summer instead of shopping abroad for the biggest deals?

One reason could be the temptation for players who are proven in the Premier League.

Many of last season's big-money signings - with a good chunk of them coming from the Bundesliga - failed to meet expectations or justify their transfer fee.

There have also been deals this summer involving the same clubs, possibly with accounting in mind, with Chelsea and Villa selling players to each other.

And there is also a feeling that teams abroad increase the transfer fees they are asking for when English teams - with all their TV riches - show interest in their players.

articles.title: Sebastián Cáceres firma por el Celta hasta 2030
articles.standfirst: Es el central que reclamaba Claudio Giráldez
articles.summary: Es el central que reclamaba Claudio Giráldez
articles.body: Sebastián Cáceres es el sexto fichaje de Celta. El central uruguayo de 27 años, procedente del Club América, firma por cuatro temporadas, hasta junio de 2030, a expensas del reconocimiento médico. En su club de procedencia superó los 200 partidos oficiales y conquistó tres Ligas MX consecutivas, un Campeón de Campeones y la Campeones Cup. Formado en el Liverpool de Montevideo, debutó como profesional en 2017 y dio el salto al fútbol mexicano en enero de 2020. Internacional absoluto con Uruguay desde 2022, disputó la Copa América de 2024 y ha formado parte de la selección uruguaya en el Mundial de 2026. Según indica el club vigués: “En México se asentó como uno de los defensas más fiables del campeonato gracias a su anticipación, su capacidad para defender espacios amplios y su salida limpia de balón. Cáceres llega en plena madurez competitiva y con el rodaje de quien lleva años peleando por títulos, un perfil que aportará solidez y experiencia a la zaga de Claudio Giráldez en una temporada exigente, con el equipo compitiendo en tres competiciones”. El Celta premia a Yoel Lago y le concede dorsal del primer equipo, al liberar alguno de ellos en las últimas fechas. El central llevará el número 18. El futbolista que lleva en dinámica de primer equipo más de un año, tenía ficha de filial, algo que cambió desde este 1 de septiembre. De hecho ya ha disputado con la primera plantilla 33 partidos oficiales, entre Liga, Copa y Europa League en los que marcó un gol y dio dos asistencias. Esta temporada ha participado en los tres partidos ligueros. Jones El-Abdellaoui seguirá en dinámica de primer equipo pero con ficha del filial, situación a la que se unirán Hugo Burcio y Andrés Antañón.

articles.title: Oficial: Álvaro Cortes firma por el Royal Amberes
articles.standfirst: El central, que no iba a disfrutar de minutos, se suma a la lista de canteranos que causan baja
articles.summary: El central, que no iba a disfrutar de minutos, se suma a la lista de canteranos que causan baja
articles.body: Álvaro Cortés ya es jugador del Royal Amberes. El central aragonés, de 21 años, fue traspasado al conjunto belga, según confirmó este martes por la noche el Barcelona. La operación se cerró en cerca de cuatro millones de euros. La entidad culé se guarda un porcentaje de una futura venta. Cortés, que tenía contrato con el Barça hasta junio de 2028, tuvo que dejar el equipo catalán para no ver frenada su proyección. Realizó la pretemporada con el primer equipo y Flick estaba muy satisfecho con su rendimiento, pero la gran competencia en el eje de la zaga iba a provocar que el zaragozano casi no disfrutara de minutos. El técnico alemán dispone de Pau Cubarsí, Gerard Martín, Andreas Christensen, Jules Koundé, Eric García... y el canterano iba a tener una presencia muy testimonial en el Barcelona. Tanto el club azulgrana como el joven profesional tenían claro que no podía bajar al filial y que la mejor opción para su carrera era continuar su trayectoria lejos del Spotify Camp Nou. Su destino es el Royal Amberes. Álvaro Cortés, que llegó al fútbol base azulgrana en verano de 2021, sólo intervino en un encuentro con el primer equipo azulgrana: fue la temporada pasada, el 13 de mayo, contra el Alavés. El central se suma a la lista de jóvenes jugadores culés que han tenido que dejar el Barça para seguir creciendo como profesionales este verano, como Tommy Marqués, Héctor Fort, Jofre Torrents o Iñaki Peña. Como con otros canteranos, el Barça se guarda con Cortés un porcentaje de una futura venta.

articles.title: El Málaga cierra su mercado con la incorporación de Jens Cajuste
articles.standfirst: Llega cedido con una opción de compra de ocho millones
articles.summary: Llega cedido con una opción de compra de ocho millones
articles.body: Jens Cajuste es nuevo jugador del Málaga CF. El centrocampista sueco se convierte en uno de los últimos refuerzos del conjunto blanquiazul en este mercado de fichajes y aterriza en La Rosaleda para apuntalar una posición que la dirección deportiva consideraba prioritaria. El acuerdo, adelantado por este medio, se ha cerrado en forma de cesión gratuita desde el Nápoles, con una opción de compra no obligatoria de ocho millones de euros. De esta manera, el Málaga incorpora al futbolista para la presente temporada sin asumir ningún coste por el préstamo y mantiene abierta la posibilidad de hacerse con sus derechos a partir del próximo verano. A sus 27 años, Cajuste responde al perfil de centrocampista defensivo que buscaba el conjunto de Martiricos. Su posición natural es la de pivote, aunque su capacidad física y versatilidad le permiten desempeñarse en diferentes zonas del centro del campo. Internacional absoluto con Suecia y con pasaporte estadounidense, el nuevo jugador malaguista pertenece al Nápoles, entidad a la que llegó procedente del Stade de Reims por 11,5 millones de euros. El futbolista mantiene contrato con el conjunto italiano hasta 2028. Cajuste cuenta, además, con experiencia en el fútbol inglés. Las dos últimas temporadas las ha disputado como cedido en el Ipswich Town. En su primer curso en la Premier League participó en 30 encuentros, 25 de ellos como titular. La pasada campaña, ya en Championship, volvió a disputar otros 30 partidos, aunque con un papel menos protagonista: fue titular en 13 ocasiones. Con su llegada, el Málaga incorpora músculo, recorrido y capacidad defensiva a su centro del campo y completa una de las operaciones que tenía marcadas como prioritarias en el tramo final del mercado.

articles.title: Rice coach Scott Abell says opener vs. Houston Christian will provide answers for Owls
articles.summary: Scott Abell is looking to become the first Rice coach to win his first two season openers in more than 35 years.
articles.body:
Like a majority of the college football programs across the nation, the 2026 Rice season begins this weekend.

For the Owls, their campaign begins against Houston Christian at 6 p.m. at Rice Stadium.

"There's more juice this week, we get an opener before our home crowd," second-year Owls head coach Scott Abell said. "I love Week 1. It's an opportunity to reflect on how the team has come together.

"We will see if we accomplished what we needed to in camp. This Saturday will answer a lot of our questions."

Abell is looking to become the first Owls head coach to win his first two season openers since Fred Goldsmith. Under Goldsmith, Rice defeated SMU 35-6 in Dallas in 1989, his debut as a head coach, and then beat Wake Forest 33-17 at home the following season.

In Abell's first season at Rice, the Owls finished 5-8 overall and 2-6 in the American.

One major difference in year 2 from year 1 at Rice is Abell plans on seeing a lot of Owls in action throughout the season.

"We are going to be committed to playing a lot of guys on Saturday," Abell said.

One of the biggest position changes for Rice in 2026 is Quinton Jackson switching from running back to receiver.

A redshirt senior from Fort Worth North Crowley, the 5-foot-9, 175-pounder has been impactful in his Owls tenure, whether it be running the ball, catching passes out of the backfield, or in kickoff returns.

A year ago, Jackson led the Owls in rushing (889 yards), all-purpose yards (1,225) and kickoff return yardage (262), tying for the team lead with seven touchdowns.

Jackson's role has changed in 2026, but not his attitude.

"In year five, I want to finish this year the right way," Jackson said. "I want to win football games and win a (conference) championship in my final year. I want to do my part for the team, whether it's running routes or blocking down the field."

Two players Abell said that have not been talked about a lot that are expected to be major contributors are a pair of transfers in tight end Preston Zinter (Notre Dame) and safety Koa Akui (Sacramento State).

Zinter (6-1, 254) played mostly on special teams for the Fighting Irish. The redshirt junior is expected to be impactful in the blocking scheme as well as catching the ball.

Akui (5-10, 193) is a graduate student, coming off an All-Big Sky selection in 2025, when he was second on the team with 65 tackles.

"Akui is always around the football," Abell said. "We are going to be physical and those two guys match that."

Saturday's opponent Houston Christian won its season opener 34-28 last Thursday at Southeastern Louisiana.

"HCU got a game under its belt," Abell said. "They are coming in with a lot of confidence."

The Huskies' Jayven Anderson, Lukasz Smolen and Cutter Stewart swept the Southland Conference's weekly awards in Week 0.

Six of Anderson's nine tackles were for loss. He was credited with a sack, one forced fumble and a blocked field goal. Stewart rushed for a game-high 95 yards and added a pair of touchdown passes. Five of his 10 completions were for at least 15 yards with a long of 66 yards to Jamaal Hall II for a score.

Smolen did double duty for the Huskies. He was 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts (30, 32 yards) and 4-for-4 on extra-point attempts. He punted twice in the win, averaging 44.5 yards.

The 2006 Rice football team, which made an improbable run following a slow start to the season to end a 45-year bowl hiatus, will be recognized this weekend.

Rice began 1-5 that year before winning six consecutive regular-season games. The journey concluded with a 41-17 loss to Troy in the New Orleans Bowl.

Activities begin Friday night at the annual Huddle Up event, followed by on-field recognition during Saturday's game.

articles.title: BVB into round two with Inacio brace and emphatic win
articles.summary: With Alexander Meyer, who was born just outside Hamburg, in goal and a total of seven personnel changes compared to the Bundesliga match against HSV (2:0), B...
articles.body:
With Alexander Meyer, who was born just outside Hamburg, in goal and a total of seven personnel changes compared to the Bundesliga match against HSV (2:0), BVB controlled the game and created chances early on – Inacio three times, all just wide – but initially overall lacked directness. The build-up play around the Oberliga side's penalty area was too slow and too predictable at first.

For over half an hour, Eimsbüttel defended countless BVB attacks with great effort before the Black-and-Yellows took the lead in the 33rd minute through an own goal by captain Wrede of all people. Julian Ryerson, BVB's top provider from last Bundesliga season, set up that goal – and the next three before halftime as well. Svensson, who repeatedly stepped out of the back three and appeared far up the pitch, bundled a Ryerson cross over the line three minutes after the opener, and Inacio then grabbed his first professional brace (41st/45+2).

Regular starters Ryerson and Felix Nmecha stayed in the dressing room after the break and were replaced by Maxi Beier and Carney Chukwuemeka. Fabio Silva made it 5:0 against the fifth-tier side after being set up by Veerman from a position that looked offside (59th minute). The game no longer had the highest intensity after that. Even so, with the shot count at 36:2 (as of the 85th minute), there were plenty of chances to add to the scoreline.

The draw for the second round of the cup will take place next Saturday from around 5:55 p.m. (live on Das Erste).

articles.title: Big Spring Pathway cancels football game against Coleman
articles.summary: The Coleman Bluecats are searching for a replacement opponent after their Friday night game against Big Spring Pathway was canceled Tuesday.
articles.body:
Less than a week after the Big Spring Pathway Warriors kicked off their high school's inaugural season of Texas high school football, the team's schedule for the rest of the 2026 season has been thrown into flux.

The Warriors played their first varsity game last Friday, a 50-6 loss to the Munday Moguls at Scruggs Field in Munday.

Big Spring Pathway's path forward, however, is full of uncertainty.

Less than 96 hours before kickoff of its Week 2 non-district matchup against Coleman, Big Spring Pathway (0-1) announced it was canceling its game against the Bluecats which had been scheduled for 7 p.m. Friday, Sept. 4, at Hufford Field in Coleman.

Coleman Independent School District officials confirmed the scheduling change to the Reporter-News on Tuesday afternoon.

Matt Stepp of Dave Campbell's Texas Football was first to report the news on X .

The Warriors have three more non-district games listed on the schedule through the end of September: a Friday night road game against Lubbock Christian (Sept. 11), a Saturday afternoon matchup against the Jal (New Mexico) Panthers (Sept. 19) at Big Spring's Memorial Stadium and a Friday night road game versus San Saba (Sept. 25) to close out their non-district slate.

Big Spring Pathway is the latest among a growing list of charter schools throughout the Lone Star State that have canceled early-season, non-district Texas high school football games this year.

Pathway joins Mesquite PTAA, Hampton Prep and Dallas Gateway as Texas based prep schools who have canceled varsity football games since the latest round of UIL realignment earlier this year.

Mesquite PTAA and Hampton Prep have withdrawn from the UIL entirely, while Dallas Gateway forfeited their Week 1 game last weekend.

The Warriors are slated to begin District 3-2A DI competition against district rivals Crosbyton, Lockney, Ralls, Roscoe and Tahoka starting in Week 7 when Big Spring Pathway visits the Lockney Longhorns (Oct. 9).

The Bluecats, meanwhile, are actively searching for a Week 2 replacement opponent for this weekend, Coleman coach Zach Edington confirmed to the Reporter-News on Tuesday.

Coleman (1-0) earned a hard-fought 16-12 win over San Angelo Grape Creek in its season opener last Friday.

Edington and the Bluecats are actively looking for a West Texas or DFW-based team to replace Big Spring Pathway as their Week 2 opponent.

Coleman's remaining non-district schedule includes home games against Abilene TLCA (Sept. 11) and Albany (Sept. 18), as well as a road matchup against Eldorado (Sept. 25).

The Bluecats also currently have a bye week scheduled for the first week of October during Week 6 of the 2026 Texas high school football season.

articles.title: Transfer deadline day live updates: Enzo Fernandez, Lamine Camara, Folarin Balogun and more done deals, latest rumors
articles.summary: The Sporting News is tracking every Deadline Day deal as the 2026 summer transfer window nears a dramatic close.
articles.body:
Every summer, Transfer Deadline Day brings thrills, excitement, and promise to many clubs throughout the Premier League and all of Europe.

Even with the 2026/27 season already under way, clubs have been able to secure outside talent and bring players into the mix, both superstars and squad contributors alike.

Top Premier League clubs have spent big money already on the likes of Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson, Bradley Barcola, and many other star players, but there are still funds to be spent before the transfer window slams shut. Teams like Tottenham, Everton , Chelsea , and even defending champions Arsenal have been linked to other players who could join before the registration period ends.

Outside of Europe, other top clubs like Barcelona , Real Madrid , PSG, and many other big-name sides are looking to keep wheeling and dealing all the way up until the very end.

The Sporting News is tracking every Deadline Day deal as the transfer window nears a dramatic close.

Man City reject Man United enquiry for Ait-Nouri

4:48 p.m. - Almost into the final hour and here's a mad one. Rayan Ait-Nouri finds himself down the pecking order at Manchester City , with Josko Gvardiol and Nico O'Reilly both preferred to him at left-back by Enzo Maresca so far this season. According to The Times, Ait-Nouri's agent offered his client to rivals Manchester United a few days ago. United followed up on that today, asking for a loan deal, but City would only agree to a loan if there was an obligation to buy the former Wolves man at the end of it. It means Tony Coton in 1996 remains the last player to move directly from City to United.

DEAL AGREED: Chelsea close in on Fernandez replacement

4:30 p.m. - Chelsea have agreed a deal in the region of $63.75m for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara. Maybe the Balogun-to-Everton deal falling through has helped to grease the wheels there, who knows. What's certain is Chelsea have their Enzo Fernandez replacement, with the Argentina international's move to Manchester City soon to be finalised.

Talking of the Balogun fiasco, Everton are now moving for Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee, who has seen potential moves to Juventus and Fiorentina fall by the wayside.

DONE DEAL! City sign Ndiaye from Everton

4:01 p.m. - One down, one to go for Manchester City. Iliman Ndiaye has joined the 10-time English champions on a five-year contract. The deal could be worth up to $87.8m. Now there are a couple of hours to get Enzo Fernandez wrapped up.

Well, there's a little longer. You see, after 9 p.m. UK time, two hours before the deadline, clubs can deploy the Deal Sheet. This is a mechanism by which teams can register their intention to complete a transfer before the deadline and get two more hours to wrap things up by 1 a.m. The way things are going this evening, we could have a few deal sheets flying around.

3:55 p.m. - Yep, we have a saga. As reported by RMC Sport, Everton medical staff believe they have found an anomaly during Balogun's medical tests. Monaco and the player's entourage contest this. It doesn't feel like an ideal state of affairs with the deadline a couple of hours away.

3:18 p.m. - We still don't know where Malick Fofana is going, after the Lyon youngster took a medical that either Sunderland or Crystal Palace will pick up the tab on. Fofana's Belgian compatriot Dodi Lukebakio is also apparently on Sunderland's radar, but they definitely have a reinforcement at the other end of the field. Kevin Danso has joined on a season-long loan from Tottenham. Chelsea's Tosin Adarabioyo is expected to take Danso's place at Spurs.

2:55 p.m. - Hold up, there could be a twist in the Folarin Balogun deal. Everton have an agreement in place worth in excess of £50m. But L'Equipe is reporting that tying up Iliman Ndiaye sale to Manchester City is taking longer than expected, meaning Everton might run out of time to seal the Balogun transfer. Surely not? Don't these people have staff?!

2:20 p.m. - Nick Woltemade had a hand in Newcastle's 2-0 win at Tottenham on Sunday and that looks like a farewell. Matias Fernandez-Pardo's arrival from Lille and Yoane Wissa's resurgent form have left the Germany international free to join Juventus on a season-long loan. Beto is also Serie A-bound and has joined Fiorentina from Everton, who anticipate Folarin Balogun's arrival to be sealed in the coming hours.

Ethan Nwaneri isn't a striker, but he can go in this post too. After spending time at Marseille last season, the Arsenal youngster is on his way to Borussia Dortmund on loan.

2:06 p.m. - Liverpool fans look set to be left in a state of uncertainty at the end of this transfer window. Their squad is talented, Bradley Barcola is a marquee arrival. but they lack a specialist right-winger and the squad looks thin in central midfield and at right-back. There is some low-key activity at Anfield today, though. Harvey Elliott has joined Valencia on loan, hoping for a more successful jaunt in La Liga than his unhappy stay at Aston Villa provided last term. Highly-rated goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans has signed from Genk for £30m but will return to the Belgian club on loan this season. Reportedly a target for Real Madrid as well, Brughmans has penned a six-year contract on Merseyside.

12:50 p.m. - Reporting earlier in the day suggested that Chelsea would only sanction a move for Fernandez if they had a replacement lined up. As of now, that does not appear to be the case, with the massive fee on the table and the players desire to leave ultimately persuading them to give the green flag. Roma's Manu Kone and Monaco's Lamine Camara are players thought to be on their radar, but the deadline is a little over five hours away.

City to equal British transfer record with Fernandez signing

12:05 p.m. - Transfer market experts David Ornstein and Fabrizio Romano are reporting that City and Chelsea have finally reached an agreement for Enzo Fernandez to move to Manchester. The fee will be £125m ($169m), equalling the British record outlay Liverpool sanctioned to sign Alexander Isak from Newcastle 12 months ago. Prior to that, Fernandez's £106.8m move to Chelsea from Benfica in January 2023 was the most expensive in British history. The Argentina midfielder is the first player in history to move for in excess of £100m twice.

11:35 a.m. - As per The Times, wantaway Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta will stay at Selhurst Park until at least January, when he will be into the final six months of his contract. It's a messy situation, with Palace having rebuffed offers from Aston Villa in the past two windows, while Mateta has also been in dispute with Palace of the contract extension that was triggered for this season. A proposed move to AC Milan collapsed in January afer he failed a medical, although the France striker returned to scored the winning goal as Palace beat Rayo Vallecano 1-0 in the Conference League final.

DONE DEAL! Newcastle seal Fernandez-Pardo deal

10:00 a.m. - Newcastle might now have wrapped up a really tidy window, one that didn't look at all likely when Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and boss Eddie Howe headed through the exit door. But four points out of six so far under new head coach Matthias Jaissle have restored a feel-good factor at St James' Park and Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo is the latest man to want in on it.

The versatile attacker joins from Lille for $69m. The Ligue 1 club have raked in plenty for their young talents during this window, having driven a hard bargain before signing off on Ayyob Bouaddi joining Manchester City for $115.1m.

9:01 a.m. - Gabriel Jesus has completed his move to Barcelona , who have paid Arsenal a reported fee of around $16m. The Brazilian has signed a three-year deal.

9:00 a.m. - The biggest projected deal of the day involves Enzo Fernandez. The Argentina midfielder is wanted by Manchester City and is eager to reunite with former boss Enzo Maresca. Chelsea appear content to sell, but only if they are able to bring in a replacement.

According to Ben Jacobs , that is the biggest issue holding up the transfer right now.

DONE DEAL: Another new signing for Aston Villa

7:55 a.m. - Aston Villa's squad overhaul continues! They have finally completed a deal for long-term target Taylor Harwood-Bellis. The defender joins from Southampton for around $40.6m.

DONE DEAL: Arsenal outcast heads for Hamburg

7:10 a.m. - Fabio Vieira, who hasn't played a Premier League game for Arsenal since 2023/24, is off to Hamburg, where he spent last season on loan. The fee is in the region of $10.8m.

DONE DEAL: An Honest agreement for Chelsea, Palace

6:55 a.m. - Chelsea have signed Honest Ahanor from Atalanta for a reported fee of $54m. However, he won't actually play for the Blues until 2027; instead, he will go on loan to Crystal Palace.

8:26 a.m. - UPDATE: Palace have now announced the season-long loan of Ahanor.

DONE DEAL: Aston Villa sign Ibrahim Mbaye for $63.6m

6:39 a.m. - What a deal is this is for Villa! Paris Saint-Germain youngster Ibrahim Mbaye joins the Premier League club for a fee of around $63.6m. The teenager joins after Villa's interest in Rafael Leao ended last week.

RUMOR: Palace hijack Sunderland deal to sign Arsenal target Fofana

5:39 am. - Well, this one took a turn! Arsenal had looked like securing a deal for Malick Fofana today, but the Lyon winger is now heading for a Sunderland medical, David Ornstein reports .

8:39 a.m. - This is becoming quite the saga: Crystal Palace are now in talks directly with Fofana and trying to convince him to join them ahead of Sunderland, Sky Sports are saying...

RUMOR: Chelsea make offer for Lamine Camara

5:39 am. - Fabrizio Romano is reporting that Chelsea have made an offer to Monaco for midfielder Lamine Camara. Although the €45m ($52m / £38m) bid is said to be too low, this is a deal that could well get done before the deadline if Enzo Fernandez joins Man City.

5:32 a.m. - Hull City have completed the signing of Ilyas Ansah from Union Berlin. Florian Plettenberg previously reported the fee was worth €24 million (£20.6m / $27.8m).

RUMOR: Chelsea trying to sign Manu Kone from Roma

5:28 a.m. - Sky in Italy are reporting that Chelsea want to push through a last-minute deal to sign midfielder Manu Kone from Roma. This appears to have come from initial discussions between the clubs about a possible loan for Jamie Gittens. However, Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini has reportedly made it clear he does not want the club to sell Kone today.

DONE DEAL: Marc Guiu joins RB Leipzig from Chelsea

5 a.m. - Chelsea remain the masters of selling players. Striker Marc Guiu has joined RB Leipzig, with the fee reported by Fabrizio Romano to be £15 million ($20.3 million). That represents decent profit on a player signed for less than half that amount two years ago.

3 a.m. — Welcome to coverage from The Sporting News of Transfer Deadline Day at the conclusion of the 2026 summer transfer window!

While plenty of big-money business has already been completed, there are still many top deals still reportedly in the works. We're tracking stories such as Folarin Balogun to Everton, Julian Alvarez to Barcelona, Enzo Fernandez to Man City, and many more!

Biggest completed transfers on deadline day

*Will join Chelsea in 2027 # Returns to Genk on loan, will join Liverpool in 2027

What time does the transfer window close?

The transfer deadline for Premier League clubs falls on Tuesday, September 1 at 11 p.m. local time (6 p.m. ET). The deadline for Spain's top clubs in La Liga is one minute before that on the same day, while Italy has a 2 p.m. ET deadline on September 1.

The deadlines in France and Germany are exactly 24 hours earlier than the one for Serie A teams.

The Dutch Eredivisie window closes on September 2, two days before the deadline for Turkish Super Lig clubs to make signings.

Transfer deadline day, time for Summer 2026

When does the Saudi Arabia transfer window close?

The window for clubs in the Saudi Pro League closes a little later than in Europe's major leagues, shutting on October 12 .

Even though the Pro League has collectively dialled back its huge spending, this creates a useful period of time for players who have not secured a move within Europe to get on the move.

The MLS extended its secondary transfer window to run from July 13 to September 2 to further align with the wider global soccer schedule.

MLS will eventually be shifting to a fully European calendar starting next summer.

articles.title: Ndiaye's journey from non-league football to £65m Man City move
articles.summary: Manchester City sign winger Iliman Ndiaye from Everton in a deal worth up to £65m.
articles.body:
Iliman Ndiaye's journey to Manchester City has been something of a scenic route after he completed a move to Etihad Stadium from Everton in a deal worth up to £65m.

The deadline day move for the Senegal winger, 26, is worth £60m plus a further £5m in add-ons - a little over six years since he made his professional debut playing in the seventh tier of English football.

"I've worked my whole life for an opportunity like this," said Ndiaye, who has signed a five-year contract with the club.

"City are one of the best clubs in the world and I've seen them win everything as I've grown up. To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I'm determined to grab it with both hands."

Ndiaye had held talks with Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal earlier in the summer while Tottenham had agreed terms with Everton on Friday night for Ndiaye, when it looked as though Richarlison would move the other way in a separate transfer.

However, sources indicated Richarlison failed to agree personal terms with his former club and as a result, Spurs were unable to proceed with the Ndiaye transfer.

The move comes on the same day City agreed to pay a joint-British transfer record fee of £125m for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

The Argentian international is set to become City's eighth summer arrival with Enzo Maresca's side having also signed Elliot Anderson, Geronimo Rulli, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Allan Elias, Jeremy Monga and Pierce Charles.

Ndiaye's journey from non-league football to City

As a 19-year-old living in London, Ndiaye was in the youth ranks of Boreham Wood and playing Sunday league football when he was invited for a one-week trial with Sheffield United.

Two trial games were enough for the then-Premier League club to sign the talented teenager, although it would be another 18 months until he made an appearance for the Blades.

Instead, he spent the second half of the 2019-20 campaign on loan at Hyde United in the Northern Premier Division, six levels below the top division.

He made six appearances in his very first taste of professional football, often risking missing the last train back to Sheffield to stay out on the training pitch.

"It's not always been easy in my career," said Ndiaye.

"But I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I'm here."

After returning to Bramall Lane, Ndiaye made his Premier League debut in March 2021 against Leicester City but it would be another three-and-a-half years until he became established at the highest level following the Blades' relegation.

Two seasons in the Championship culminated in Ndiaye spearheading their return to the top flight in 2023 with 14 goals in 43 starts but he was then sold to Marseille that summer.

Ndiaye struggled during a season in France before joining Everton for an initial £16m fee in July 2024.

A firm fan favourite on Merseyside, "Skiliman" scored 15 goals and provided four assists in 67 Premier League games for the Toffees before his City move.

In a summer of highly-inflated transfer fees, value has become increasingly hard to determine.

On one hand, the Senegal international is a player of superlative skill, evasive, quick and wonderfully entertaining with the ball at his feet.

Ndiaye was responsible for 73 of Everton's 250 completed dribbles last season, the highest share of any Premier League player.

Everton fans may also point to recent moves in the Premier League involving City, such as the sale of Savio to Tottenham for an initial £75m, as further evidence that the club should have demanded more for Ndiaye.

On the other hand, Everton are effectively quadrupling the initial £16m they paid Marseille to sign Ndiaye two years ago for a player whose underlying numbers, at this stage at least, are not truly elite.

In the Premier League last season, Ndiaye only ranked joint third at Everton alone for goal contributions (nine), with Beto (10) and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (12) providing more.

It is reasonable to assume that those numbers for Ndiaye will improve in a more attacking team at City but his general creativity is also middling as things stand.

He created 36 chances in total in the Premier League last season, ranking him only fourth at Everton. Toffees midfielder James Garner created 26 more. Jack Grealish, whose season ended in January because of injury, created eight more.

Grealish has effectively replaced Ndiaye at Everton following his loan move from Enzo Maresca's side.

Casting the net a little wider, 45 Premier League players have recorded more goal contributions than Ndiaye's 19 since he made his Everton debut two years ago.

As a 26-year-old set to be surrounded by better players, it would be no surprise should his numbers flourish at the Etihad.

But even in today's money, £65m for Ndiaye's current output may not be as questionable a deal as it sounds.

articles.title: County Antrim Shield: Glens beat Blues to progress as holders Carrick bow out
articles.summary: Glentoran are the comfortable 3-1 victors over Linfield at the Oval in the first round of the County Antrim Shield, while holders Carrick Rangers exited after being defeated by Crusaders.
articles.body:
Glentoran were the comfortable 3-1 victors over Linfield at the Oval in the first round of the County Antrim Shield, while holders Carrick Rangers exited after being defeated by Crusaders after a penalty shootout.

Jordan Jenkins struck twice inside the opening six minutes to hand the home side a dream start in east Belfast before Charlie Chapman's early second-half strike threatened a Linfield fightback.

The Blues could not find a way back level after Cal Weatherup restored the home side's two-goal advantage.

At Seaview, Jacob Blaney and Owen Wardell gave the Crues a comfortable lead before an impressive final five minutes from the holders forced the tie to be decided on penalties.

However, Declan Caddell's side were the 5-4 victors in the penalty shootout to book their spot in the next round.

Jenkins double shoots down youthful Blues

The home side could not have asked for a better start, taking the lead inside two minutes when James Douglas held off the Linfield defence and diverted the ball into the path of Jenkins, who fired low into the bottom corner past a helpless Aidan Glavin.

That set the tone, and the east Belfast side doubled their advantage soon after, as Daniel Larmour nodded Ryan Cooney's free-kick across goal for Jenkins to slot home from close range for his second of the evening.

The Glens settled into their passing rhythm from there and should have extended their lead after the half-hour, when Cooney picked out Josh Kelly unmarked on the edge of the box, but the midfielder could not beat Glavin in the Linfield goal.

However, Linfield came out fighting after the break and almost had an immediate reward when Dylan Wells' curling 25-yard free-kick beat Crellin, only to cannon back off the near post.

They went close again soon after, Wells this time whipping a free-kick to the far post for Donatas Jermakovas, who rose highest but could only flash his header wide.

The Linfield pressure eventually told when Chapman picked up possession at the back post and earned himself a yard of space before firing past Billy Crellin at the near post.

However, there was to be no fightback as the home side restored their two-goal cushion when Cooney's long throw was flicked on at the near post and substitute Weatherup bundled it over the line to ensure the Glens' progression into the next round.

Ballymacash Rangers 0-6 Ballymena United

articles.title: West Ham 4-2 Wolves: Nuno's side claim first Championship win of the season
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between West Ham United and Wolverhampton Wanderers at the London Stadium on Tuesday night; Divine Mukasa scores twice as Nuno's Hammers claim their first league win of the season.
articles.body:
Wolves, who also went down from the Premier League last term, could have gone top with a victory but ended up losing for the first time under new manager Cesar Peixoto.

Jarrod Bowen and Konstantinos Mavropanos also scored for the hosts, with Marshall Munetsi and Mavropanos' own goal replying for Wolves.

The win eased the pressure on manager Nuno Espirito Santo on a night when Amanda Staveley, who is heading a consortium looking to buy a significant stake in West Ham, was at the London Stadium.

West Ham struggled initially and were relieved when Raul Jimenez, picked out in space in the box by Jackson Tchatchoua, shanked wildly wide.

Jimenez's next attempt, from a corner played almost to the edge of the box, was better though. The Mexico striker's shot bounced off the turf, over goalkeeper Mads Hermansen and on to the top of the crossbar.

Mateus Mane also hit the bar not long afterwards, from the left of the box after Kyle Walker-Peters had failed to cut out a cross. The full-back recovered to get just enough of a deflection on the shot that followed.

A goal was coming and it was the hosts who scored it against the run of play in the 33rd minute.

Mukasa, the on-loan Manchester City midfielder, unleashed a rising drive from more than 20 yards that went in off the underside of the crossbar.

West Ham were a team transformed, with Munetsi having to block on the line from Max Kilman.

And they were awarded a penalty in the 40th minute for Andre's lunge on Joel Piroe. Bowen sent goalkeeper Jose Sa the wrong way to slot home.

Wolves hit back in the 43rd minute when Munetsi won a chase with Mavropanos that saw him turn the Greek defender and end a low drive beyond Hermansen's dive to his left.

West Ham increased their lead in the 53rd minute through Mukasa. The teenager accepted Bowen's pass from the right and saw his shot loop off the boot of Nasser Djiga to leave Sa helpless again.

Sa batted away a Bowen drive from an angle but West Ham made it 4-1 in the 64th minute through Mavropanos' goal from the resulting corner. The centre-back saw his header deflected on to the crossbar but lashed home the rebound, also off the bar.

Wolves pulled a goal back in the 69th minute when Mavropanos, sliding in to stop Tchatchoua setting up substitute Jordan James, diverted the ball into his own net.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Preston 1-3 Bristol City: Robins win piles more misery on North End
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Preston North End and Bristol City at Deepdale on Tuesday night; Scott Twine, Lisav Eissat and Dominic Ballard score as Robins claim victory and pile more misery on the Lilywhites.
articles.body:
Scott Twine had tapped City into a fourth-minute lead but the Lilywhites fought back strongly and Caleb Wiley slammed them level with a 51st-minute rocket.

Lisav Eissat's looping 79th-minute header crushed North End hearts before Dom Ballard coolly bagged his second goal of the season, albeit less spectacularly than his stunner against Birmingham, to secure the victory seven minutes later.

The night started woefully for the hosts as Lorent Tolaj picked out Twine with an inviting centre and the ex-Burnley man gobbled up from close range with a first-time finish.

Despite the shocking start, North End should have levelled minutes later as Jusef Erabi failed to properly connect with Liam Lindsay's inch-perfect delivery with the goal gaping.

The hosts continued to take the game to their opponents and went close twice in quick succession as Sam Tickle did well to turn Jordan Thompson's free-kick over the bar before Delano Burgzorg beat the 24-year-old with a header across the goal from Harry Clarke's cross, only to be denied by the foot of a post.

Those early chances seemed to wake the Robins up and former Preston loanee Sam Greenwood stung the palms of Daniel Iversen with a 25th-minute snapshot from the edge of the box having been teed up by Twine.

Nonetheless, an all-action Thompson was trying his best to drag his side level, thundering a 30-yard howitzer narrowly over the bar in the 35th minute while Greenwood again fired straight into Iversen's hands.

Wind kept very much in the sails of Paul Heckingbottom's men after the break and they could have scored twice before they did, Clarke heading Thompson's corner wide from close range and then through Alfie Devine, who failed on several occasions to pull the trigger in the box before eventually being blocked by Tickle.

But that pressure eventually did pay dividends as Wiley caught everybody by surprise with a sensational drive from range that nestled into the corner.

Preston fans were even more buoyant on the 68th minute as a big screen announcement confirmed they had signed two new players on deadline day but that euphoria almost turned sour within a minute as Tolaj broke clear on goal, only for Iversen's leg to keep out his effort.

Michael Skubala's team were steadily growing back into the game and killed Preston off with two late sucker punches.

Eissat expertly looped Rio Cardines' free-kick out of Iversen's reach to put his team ahead and Ballard pounced on some suspect defending to round the goalkeeper and score a third, condemning Preston to a fourth straight loss.

What the result means and next fixtures...
